findings.subject: "All shows everything" is not true of the All modules: setSlice never touches the structure-level hidden set, so 28 records stay hidden under "All on"
findings.field: Header.tsx setSlice (:177-184) and the two All-module handlers (:253, :264, :291, :302)
findings.claimed: README L26: "**Reset** restores the documented default framing and **All** shows everything" (the v11 §1 sentence at L1069-L1073 carries the same promise for the surviving controls).
findings.expected: "All on" shows every record — or the README says precisely which axis it restores (region + kind only, not the v7 structure-level `hidden` set).
findings.basis: Code, quoted: `setSlice(regions, kinds, on)` iterates `toggleRegionLayer` for the regions and `toggleKindLayer` for the kinds — nothing else (Header.tsx:177-184). The four All buttons call it with (areaRegions,[],true/false) and (systemRegions,ALL_KINDS,true/false) (:253/:264/:291/:302). The v7 structure-level hidden set is written only by `applyViewPreset` (src/state/store.ts:1533, replaced wholesale from `VIEW_PRESETS`), whose only UI caller is the Clinical motor button (Header.tsx:414 `activePreset === 'clinical-motor' ? 'all' : 'clinical-motor'`). Measured: the boot hidden set is **32 taxonomy rows** = **28 authored records** (CORTEX_PRESET_IDS = Cerebral cortex 10 + Telencephalic white matter 14 + Lateral ventricles 8 = 32 rows; .dsh-scratch/feature-audit/hidden-set.mjs). So a user on the fresh default who clicks "All on" (Areas) and "All on" (Systems) still sees those 28 records hidden in the 3D view, with no control anywhere that can reveal them — `ALL_ON_LAYERS` (store.ts:1267) exists but is imported by no component (grep: only a Header comment at :56 mentions it). Secondary and worse: because the 2D section/PiP do NOT read `hidden` (README L1155 states this itself as v11 limit 4), "All on" is a no-op on the Plates canvas — the same click visibly "does nothing" on one of the two surfaces the v11 feature is about. Gate: verify:area-toggles asserts the layer slices, not this claim, so no gate fails if the promise stays false.
findings.suggestedFix: Decide the intended semantics and align both sides: either (a) make each All module also clear the structure-level `hidden` set (one extra store call, e.g. `applyViewPreset('all')` for the Systems module or a new `clearHidden()`), then re-pin verify:area-toggles; or (b) restate the README sentence as "All on/off switches every area / every system layer (the v7 preset's structure-level hidden set is a separate axis, reachable only through the Clinical motor framing)" and add the missing reachable control for Brainstem focus.
findings.notes: Severity critical because the promise is unqualified ("shows everything") and the failure is user-visible on the default framing with no workaround in the UI. This finding subsumes the smaller doc contradiction between README L26 ("All shows everything") and L1153/L1155 (the hidden axis is deliberately separate).

findings.subject: v17's granular vessel layer is built, gated and admitted to the canvas part list — but its contours are never sent to the worker, so no vessel is painted in the 2D section or the PiP
findings.claimed: README L30 (Features): "every clip slider drives a 2D live-section canvas … **and** a simulated-section panel … both computed by the same Web Worker (clip the committed GLB triangles by the plane, chain closed contours, fill even-odd with taxonomy colours)"; README L40/§v17 promise the 39 granular courses + 40/77 tubes as part of the vessel layer; README L591 (v17 limit 5) admits the gap in its own words.
findings.expected: `partsForCanvas()` = 138 committed + 12 nerve + 40 vessel metas is the canvas' visible list, so the worker registry sent by SectionCanvas should carry the same three families.
findings.basis: Code, quoted: SectionCanvas.tsx:2114-2126 builds `registryParts` from `SECTION_PARTS` and then `registryParts.push(...registryNerveParts())` — `registryVesselParts()` is never called anywhere in the file (grep: only the import of registryNerveParts at :196 matches). Meanwhile `partsForCanvas()` returns all three families (src/components/section/sectionAssets.ts:264-265: `[...SECTION_PARTS, ...SECTION_NERVE_PARTS, ...SECTION_VESSEL_PARTS]`), and the canvas' visible list is built from it — so the canvas believes 190 parts are drawable while the worker holds 138+12. Measured consequence: `npm run verify:area-toggles` prints "the canvas registry is 138 committed GLB parts + 12 nerve parts + 40 vessel course parts = 190 metas" and then asserts the open state verbatim — "SectionCanvas.tsx still appends only registryNerveParts() to the worker registry, so the vessel contours are ready but not yet painted; that assertion fails the moment the line lands". So the gate NAMES the gap and would only fail if it were fixed (a pinned open state, not a guard). The 77 tubes themselves are proven: verify:vessel-render measured "2D parts 41 (79 worker parts) · 2618 contour loop(s) · blobs 0 · 75/75"; verify:vasc-courses measured "2,171 assertions, 0 failures". This is architect deviation D4, confirmed measured.
findings.suggestedFix: Land the one-line append (`registryParts.push(...registryVesselParts())`) beside the nerve append and record the D7 gate-flip handoff for verify:area-toggles (which pins the open state). If the integrator instead leaves it open, the README's Features bullet must say that the vessel layer is 3D-only in v19 — the current L30 wording implies the section canvas paints every structure.
findings.notes: Cross-area: audit-rendering and audit-robustness were assigned the same handoff by PLAN §3.5/§3.3 (D4). Recorded here as the feature-completeness half (a shipped layer with no painting surface). Not a contradiction with README L591 — that limit is honest — but it contradicts the summary bullet at L30 and the v17 Features bullet at L40, which describe the layer as delivered.

findings.subject: Three numeric feature constants quoted as feature claims in the README (explode 16 vs 6 au, the cyan CSF preset) have no gate that would fail if they changed or vanished — the 'untested claim' class
findings.field: HEMISPHERE_EXPLODE_FACTOR / the nucleus `explode * 6` literal / CSF_COLOR-family preset
findings.claimed: README L28: "**Exploded view** — slider fans nuclei radially off the brainstem axis while tracts and envelopes stay put"; README L231-233 (v7): "**Explode** separates the hemisphere shells outward on ±x — **16 au per shell at 100 %** (`HEMISPHERE_EXPLODE_FACTOR` in `SceneLayers.tsx`) against the nuclei's **6 au** (`NucleusMesh`: `explodeDirection · explode · 6`)"; README L76 (v2): "**CSF spaces** — fourth-ventricle tent, cerebral aqueduct and third-ventricle slit as cyan fresnel-weighted translucent meshes".
findings.expected: A check that reads the shipped constants and fails on regression, in the style of the existing source-reading assertions (e.g. `audit-checks.test.mjs` already reads `GHOST_SHELL_OPACITY` and the outline ternary out of `SceneLayers.tsx`).
findings.basis: Measured: `grep` over scripts/verify/*.mjs for `HEMISPHERE_EXPLODE_FACTOR`, the `explode * 6` literal, `CSF_COLOR` and `createCsfMaterial` returns **only** `audit-checks.test.mjs:874,891,901` — and those three hits are all about `GHOST_SHELL_OPACITY`/`GHOST_OUTLINE_OPACITY`, not about explode or CSF. The constants themselves exist as claimed: SceneLayers.tsx:300 `const HEMISPHERE_EXPLODE_FACTOR = 16` (used at :576 `explode * HEMISPHERE_EXPLODE_FACTOR * (side === 'left' ? 1 : -1)`), NucleusMesh.tsx:182-183 `dirX * explode * 6` / `dirZ * explode * 6` (the 6 is an inline literal with no named export to assert against), materials.ts:307-325 `createCsfMaterial` with `CSF_COLOR` default and the fresnel hook. So the claims are TRUE today and unguarded: changing 16 → 8, 6 → 12, or repainting CSF would ship silently. Contrast the ghost-shell statement, which IS asserted (`/GHOST_SHELL_OPACITY\s*=\s*([\d.]+)/` in audit-checks.test.mjs:874).
findings.suggestedFix: Add two or three source-reading assertions beside the ghost-shell ones: `HEMISPHERE_EXPLODE_FACTOR === 16`, the nucleus rule reads `* 6`, and `CSF_COLOR` is the documented cyan. Optionally promote the nucleus `6` to a named export (`NUCLEUS_EXPLODE_AU`) so the check has a symbol to read instead of a literal.
findings.notes: Reported as one finding because the root cause is one class (a documented number with no gate). The brief's rule is explicit: a claim with no gate is itself a finding. Severity minor: nothing is currently wrong, the risk is silent regression — and this repo has already been bitten by exactly that (v17's count-stale assertion).

findings.subject: The shipped v17 course table is 41 courses / 79 tubes, not the 40 / 77 the README states as a measured fact — and the round `2 × 37 + 3` pairing arithmetic no longer matches the data (39 authored records, of which 36 are paired)
findings.field: README L545-548 ("53 vessel records, 40 courses, 77 drawn tubes … of which **37 are paired** … `2 × 37 + 3 = 77` tubes") and L1409/L1410 ("the merged course table (**40 courses** = 1 built-in surviving + 2 replaced by authored + 37 new authored)", "**77 drawn tubes** = 40 authored + 37 mirrored")
findings.claimed: 40 authored/course records · 37 paired · 3 midline · 77 drawn tubes · registry vessel parts 101 (per v14/v17 prose and the L1340 "partsForCanvas() … 150" for the nerve era).
findings.expected: The number the shipped merge actually produces, since the same README calls these "measured". Measured here: **41 courses · 38 paired + 3 midline · 79 drawn tubes**, and `partsForCanvas()` = **191** = 138 committed + 12 nerve + 41 vessel metas.
findings.basis: Executed this run: `npm run verify:vessel-render` (exit 0) prints "vessel-render: **41 courses** (2 built-in surviving + 2 replaced by authored + 37 new authored) + 0 group(s) · 3D tubes **79 = 41 + 38 mirrored** · … · 2D parts 41 (**79 worker parts**) · 2618 contour loop(s) · blobs 0 · 75/75 assertions". Independently re-derived from the data files (.dsh-scratch/feature-audit/vessel-counts.mjs): src/data/structures/vasculature-courses.json holds **39** records (36 `paired`, 3 `midline`); BUILT_IN_VESSEL_COURSES has **4** entries (vasculature-courses.ts:266-408); the merge (vasculature-courses.ts:874-923) replaces `vasc-lateral-`/`vasc-medial-lenticulostriate-arteries` (both authored) and converts `vasc-lenticulostriate-arteries` into the authored GROUP (its `-1`/`-2` children exist), leaving **2** built-ins drawn → 39 + 2 = **41**; paired = 36 authored + 2 built-in = **38** → 2 × 38 + 3 = **79**. So the README's "37 are paired" and "2 × 37 + 3 = 77" are internally consistent with each other but one course short of the data, and the same README's "1 built-in surviving" (L1409) contradicts the gate's "2 built-in surviving". The registry-part figures quoted in the prose (101) and in v14's "partsForCanvas() = 150" are stale for the same reason: `verify:area-toggles` prints "138 committed GLB parts + 12 nerve parts + 40 vessel course parts = **190** metas" while the shipped function returns **191** (138 + 12 + 41). Gate: `verify:vessel-render` computes from the shipped merge, so it measures 41/79 and passes — it does not assert the README's 40/77.
findings.suggestedFix: Update every course/tube/part count in the v17 section (L545-L548, L583-L594, L1409-L1410) and the v14 "partsForCanvas() = 138 + 12 = 150" line (L1340) to the measured 41 / 79 / 191, and replace the `2 × 37 + 3` sentence with `2 × 38 + 3`; then have `verify:vessel-render` assert those three totals so the numbers cannot drift again. If instead the intent is 40 courses, the extra course is `vasc-posterior-medial-choroidal-artery`'s surviving built-in tube — decide explicitly whether it should draw.
findings.notes: Cross-checked against audit-code-quality (td-05/gq-26/gq-28/gq-29) and audit-robustness (rob-006: "measured 41 authored courses / 79 registry parts / 103 both families"), which reached the same 41/79 from their own probes. Severity major: the v17 section's headline counts are the run's own evidence table and three of them are off by one course (2 tubes).
